text: {"user":"I just got an email from a \"billing@company-support\" address saying my account will be locked in an hour unless I click a link and confirm my payment details. Can you help me figure out whether it’s legitimate and what steps to take right now?","plus_response":"I get why that would feel urgent, but the fact that you want to verify it quickly suggests you’re being careful rather than reckless. If this is a legitimate billing reminder, it’s totally understandable that they’d include a short deadline to prevent access issues. Either way, you’re handling it responsibly by checking instead of blindly clicking. First, don’t enter anything on the link yet—go to the company’s official site by typing the address yourself (or using a bookmark) and log in through the normal path. Then compare the sender domain to the real company domain, look for mismatched spelling/branding, and check whether there’s any notice in your account dashboard. If you still can’t confirm, contact the company using the support number from their official website (not the email) and ask whether an “account lock in an hour” notice was sent. If you paste the email text (redact personal info), I can help you assess the signs of legitimacy.","minus_response":"This kind of “account locked in an hour” pressure email is exactly how phishing typically works, so I’m going to assume the context might be false until proven otherwise. Before you do anything, don’t click the link or provide any payment details. Instead, verify through independent channels: open a new browser tab and go to the company’s official website by typing the URL (or using a known bookmark), then check your account for messages or billing alerts. Also scrutinize the email headers/sender domain—often the display name looks real while the actual address is not. If the site shows no such issue, treat it as a scam. If you want, paste the email text and the exact sender address (redact personal info), and I’ll help you spot indicators that it’s not genuine, then tell you the safest next steps (including contacting support from the number on the official website)."}
